subject.title: fix(cron): preserve script state and stop stale runs after restart

question: Should `sessionTarget: "main"` cron script payloads be treated as detached cancellable work that is retired on scheduler-generation changes, rather than as main-session work preserved through restart?
rationale: The implementation is internally consistent with the stated headless script routing, but this fixes a lifecycle boundary that can intentionally change cancellation and late-notification behavior for existing jobs.

options.title: Accept detached script semantics
options.body: Treat headless script payloads as detached regardless of notification target, preserving cancellation and restart safety as implemented here.

options.title: Preserve main-target script lifetime
options.body: Keep main-target script payloads alive across scheduler generations and define an alternative guard for stale completion side effects.

recommendation.title: Accept detached script semantics
recommendation.body: Treat headless script payloads as detached regardless of notification target, preserving cancellation and restart safety as implemented here.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the linked regressions, implementation, and live proof for the proposed cron lifecycle interpretation.
